concerns.text: The gold‑standard intent annotation set is generated deterministically by two rule‑based extractors and κ ≥ 0.6 is guaranteed analytically. FR‑008 requires a *human‑annotated* gold standard with inter‑annotator agreement ≥ 0.6; a rule‑based proxy does not validate that the extracted “intent” entities correspond to the construct of technical intent, threatening construct validity.

If any model exceeds the 60 s CPU timeout the pipeline re‑runs **all** models on a Kaggle GPU. This hardware switch introduces a confound: models may benefit differentially from GPU acceleration (e.g., larger models may see larger speed gains), violating Principle VII’s requirement that differences be attributable solely to architecture.

The plan states a Monte‑Carlo simulation will confirm ≥80 % power for 500 pairs but provides no assumed effect size, variance estimates, or α level. Without these parameters the claim of sufficient power is unsupported, risking an under‑powered Friedman test.

Commit sampling is performed uniformly across five repositories, but no stratification or balancing for repository‑specific documentation styles, commit frequency, or domain complexity is described. Repository‑level variability could act as an uncontrolled confound affecting model performance.

Surface entity extraction relies on regex + AST verification, yet the regex patterns are fixed and may miss many legitimate surface changes (e.g., multi‑line signatures, indirect imports). Incomplete capture would bias precision/recall scores, undermining construct validity of the “surface” metric.
